summary: Menu-item text-fit measurer (__thiscall): loads a text buffer pointer from field this+0xE0 (falling back to the global byte_5EA438), then measures the text character by character with TextRenderToSurface against an available-width constraint a2, returning the character index at which the menu-item text must be truncated.

operations.description: Load the text buffer pointer stored at field this+0xE0 (this[56]); v4 = *this[56].
When the field pointer is null, fall back to the global default text source byte_5EA438.
Initialize scan index v5 = a3 + 1, equality flag v6 = (a3 + 1 == a4), and previous-width v11 = 0.
Skip the measurement loop entirely when a3 + 1 >= a4 (no characters left to measure).

Scan characters v5 from a3 + 1 upward while v5 < a4; on each iteration temporarily null-terminate the buffer at v5, measure, restore the original character, and break when the measured width reaches the available width.
Measure the rendered width of the substring &v4[a3]..v5 by calling TextRenderToSurface(&v4[a3], &a2, v12, 1); the measured width updates a2 and the previous width is saved in v11.
Break the loop when the measured width a2 is no longer less than the original available width v7 (kept before the loop).
Mid-point correction: when v7 <= (v11 + a2) / 2, step the index back one character (--v5) to compensate for the last character's over-width.
Final tail correction: when the scan reached a4 (v6), v5 > a3, and the character at v4[v5] is non-null, step v5 back by one.
Return the final character index v5 at which the menu-item text is considered to fit.
Called by MenuItemLayoutCalculator (0x0047B850) and MenuCursorPositioning (0x0047B9C0) to determine the visible text length for a menu item.
